## About us

IRAP’s scientific objectives concern the study and understanding of the Universe and its contents: the Earth as a planet, its ionized space environment, the sun and its planets, the stars and their planetary systems, the interstellar environment , galaxies, the very first stars and the primordial Big Bang.
With activities of design, construction, integration and operation of instruments on the ground and in space as well as laboratory experiments allowing the characterization of physical processes, IRAP is one of the major poles of ground-space astrophysics in France.
IRAP has numerous collaborations both regionally and internationally with organizations such as CNES, ESA, ESO, NASA, JAXA …
IRAP benefits from numerous fundings through calls for projects, notably within the framework of the National Research Agency (ANR) and the Horizon 2020 program of the European Union.

## Observer et comprendre l'Univers

## Who are we ?

IRAP teams work on the study and understanding of the Universe and its content: the Earth as a planet, its ionized spatial environment, the sun and its planets, the stars and their planetary systems, the interstellar environment, galaxies, compact objects, the very first stars and the primordial Big Bang.  
This is done through observation, modeling and theory, instrumentation and laboratory experiments.

With a staff of technical personnel qualified in the field of design, construction, integration and operation of instruments on the ground and in space, IRAP is a major center of instrumentation in astrophysics , at an international level. # Planets, Environments and Space Plasmas (PEPS)

# Planets, Environments and Space Plasmas (PEPS)

Leader: **Vincent Génot**  
Deputies: **Philippe Garnier, Jérémie Lasue**

The PEPS team members are interested in the set of processes governing the surfaces and space environments of the planets, moons and small bodies of the Solar System, as well as their interactions with the Sun and the solar wind. The developed themes are categorised into 4 main topics:

* The properties of the plasma and the magnetic field at the surface and in the solar corona, as well as the emergence and propagation of the solar wind and solar flares in the interplanetary medium. The main means of observation are the space missions [Solar Orbiter](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/solar-orbiter-pas-2/) , [Parker Solar Probe](https://www.irap.omp.eu/en/project/parker-solar-probe-2/) , [Stereo](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/en/project/stereo-swea-2/) and the [Climso](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/climso-2/) coronograph at the Pic du Midi.
* The Earth’s space environment, from its interaction with the solar wind and the Moon in the outer magnetosphere to its internal coupling with the exosphere, ionosphere and upper atmosphere. The main means of observation are the space missions [MMS](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/mms-2/) , [Cluster](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/cis-cluster-2/) , [HelioSwarm](https://www.irap.omp.eu/en/sno/helioswarm-2/) ( [Taranis,](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/taranis-idee-et-xgre-2/) failed launch in 2020), [Swarm](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/swarm-2/) and the ground [SuperDARN](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/superdarn-2/) and [Eiscat](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/eiscat-eiscat-3d-2/) radars.
* The properties of the environments of planets and small bodies of the Solar System taking into account their specificities (magnetic field, atmosphere, rings, satellites). The main past, present and future space missions are [BepiColombo](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/bepicolombo-mppe/) for Mercury, [Venus Express](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/venus-express-aspera-4/) and [EnVision](https://www.irap.omp.eu/project/envision-2/) for Venus, [MAVEN](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/maven-swea/) and [Mars Express](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/mars-express-aspera-3/) for Mars, [Juno](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/juno-jade/) and [JUICE](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/juice-pep/) for Jupiter, [Cassini](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/cassini-mimi/) for Saturn, [Rosetta](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/rosetta/) and [Comet Interceptor](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/comet-interceptor-dfp-lees/) for comets.
* The study of planetary surfaces and small bodies of the Solar System (geological evolutions, mineralogical and chemical compositions, past environments) as well as their formation and evolution. The main present and future space missions are [ChemCam/MSL-Curiosity](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/msl-chemcam-2/) , [SuperCam/Mars2020-Perseverance](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/mars-2020-supercam-2/) and [RLS/Exomars](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/exomars/) for Mars, [DORN/Chang’e 6](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/project/dorn/) for the Moon and laboratory instrument developments for Venus.

The PEPS team is deeply involved in instrumental developments of space missions, in theoretical developments and numerical modelling, in development of scientific analysis and archiving tools ( [CDPP](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/centre-de-donnees-de-la-physique-des-plasmas/) , [STORMS](https://www.irap.omp.eu/irap2/sno/storms-2/) ) and in outreach, teaching and valorisation activities towards industry and civil society (instrumental R&D, instrumental calibrations, scientific and technical expertise, [Space Weather](http://www.meteo-espace.fr/) ).
